keyVerseText: Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked of the wise men, was exceeding wroth, and sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently enquired of the wise men.
rootMeaning: The Greek adjective διετής (dietḗs) derives from the root words δὶς (dís), meaning 'twice' or 'again,' and ἔτος (étos), meaning 'year.' This etymology reveals that the word literally signifies something pertaining to a span of two years. Beyond the simple English gloss 'two years old,' the root sense emphasizes the duration or period of two complete years, highlighting a precise measure of time rather than a vague age range.
usageInScripture: The term διετής occurs only once in the New Testament, specifically in Matthew 2:16, where it is translated as 'two years old.' This consistent usage underscores the word's specificity in describing the exact age of children targeted by Herod's decree. Its singular occurrence and clear translation demonstrate that διετής is used to denote a precise age, emphasizing the historical detail of the event recorded.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding διετής as a precise measure of age grounds the biblical narrative in historical reality, affirming the reliability of Scripture's details. It reminds believers of the humanity and vulnerability of Christ as a child, who was subject to the same dangers as other children of that exact age. This specificity also reflects God's sovereign orchestration of history, where even the ages of children in a tragic event serve His redemptive purposes. Recognizing the exactness of such terms encourages a faithful trust in the Scripture's accuracy and the unfolding of God's plan in Christ.
keyVerseReflection: Matthew 2:16 recounts Herod's violent response to the wise men, ordering the killing of all male children 'from two years old and under.' The use of διετής here precisely identifies the age range of the children affected, grounding the narrative in a concrete historical timeframe. This detail conveys the extent of Herod's cruelty and the vulnerability of the Messiah's early life, deepening the reader's appreciation of the peril surrounding Jesus' infancy.
